lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: real-world diagonal problems

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A 10-ft ladder reaches 8 ft up a wall. How far is its base from the wall?

steps: Identify the legs and the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle.
Use a² + b² = c² and take a square root only after finding c².

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A student claims 5² + 12² = 17² for a right triangle. Is the claim correct?
choices: Yes; add the legs to find the hypotenuse.

items.prompt: Which is longer: a 3-by-4 rectangle diagonal or a 5-by-12 rectangle diagonal?
What does a² + b² = c² describe?
choices: the side lengths of a right triangle
the angle sum of a triangle

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: In a right triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 5 and 9. What is its hypotenuse in simplest radical form?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 5 and 4. What is its hypotenuse in simplest radical form?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
